newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Dairy Board expands lactose plant for NZ$20 mln.
newsitem.headline: NZ Dairy Board expands lactose plant for NZ$20 mln.

text.p: The New Zealand Dairy Board said on Wednesday it had approved a significant expansion of its lactose (milk sugar) processing facility in Taranaki.

The board's 100 percent owned subsidiary The Lactose Company runs the Kaponga manufacturing plant, the world's third largest with 32,000 tonnes of lactose manufactured annually. The board said the plant would be expanded to enable handling of more than 40,000 tonnes.
The expansion was already underway and would cost around NZ$20 million. It is due for completion in late August.
The Lactose Company exports to 37 countries and currently generates nearly $50 million in sales, the board said.
The majority of the extra capacity would enable the production of highly refined lactose for manufacturers of pharmaceutical products and infant formulae.
